functions.name: core_delay_ms
functions.brief: Blocking delay in milliseconds. Thread builds (Core.ST.W5): the wait runs Thread's scheduler, so Thread callbacks (UDP receive, state changes) can run inside it, and it can end up to ~1 ms late.

functions.name: core_delay_us
functions.brief: Blocking delay in microseconds. For delays > 1 ms prefer `delay_ms` — it won't starve the rest of the system as long.

functions.name: core_timeout
functions.brief: Check if a timeout has elapsed. start: value returned by core_millis() at the beginning ms:    timeout duration in milliseconds Returns 1 if expired, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: core_cycle_init
functions.brief: Enable the DWT cycle counter. Idempotent; call once at startup.

functions.name: core_delay_cycles
functions.brief: Busy-wait `cycles` CPU cycles (≈ ±a few cycles of loop overhead).

functions.name: core_delay_ns
functions.brief: Busy-wait `ns` nanoseconds (rounds to whole CPU cycles).

functions.name: hal_tick
functions.brief: Milliseconds since boot, from the SysTick counter (requires ll_systick_init).

functions.name: hal_timeout_expired
functions.brief: Wrap-safe check that timeout_ms has elapsed since the tick value start.

functions.name: ll_systick_init
functions.brief: Initialize SysTick for 1ms interrupts + delay functions. sysclk_hz: System clock frequency in Hz (e.g., 80000000 for 80MHz) After calling this, SysTick fires every 1ms and increments _systick_ticks. ll_delay_ms() uses this counter. ll_delay_us() still uses polling mode for sub-ms precision.

functions.name: ll_delay_ms
functions.brief: Blocking delay in milliseconds. Uses the SysTick interrupt counter for accurate timing.

functions.name: ll_delay_us
functions.brief: Blocking delay in microseconds. Uses a counting loop based on the known ticks-per-us. Less precise than the old SysTick-polling approach, but compatible with the interrupt-driven SysTick.
